world.laws: Local councils set their own rules. In Brineharbor, necromancy is permitted; in Shellcove, it is forbidden; in Oldsalt Harbor, it is regulated. Authorities act on witnesses, reports, and discovered evidence. Willing ancestral contact, grave theft, and unwilling soul binding are treated as different acts.
world.culture: Wild groves are protected as common ground, and moon watchers teach respect for changing seasons.

festival.name: The First Moon Fair
festival.tradition: Apprentices display their work beside the oldest local craft masters.

rumors: The academy in Brineharbor is seeking careful field observers, not only wealthy students.
A moonwise ranger near The Fox Pathwood can teach a refuge ritual without demanding allegiance.
Licensed ancestral research is attracting healers from distant villages.
Makers are needed along the road to Ember Road Bastion; honest craft can become a life’s work.
Harbor workers argue over storm repairs and the price of inland grain.
The ferrymen call the water The Vesper Run; its old crossing bells can still be heard after dusk.

event.title: A Note Asking to Meet
event.body: Someone has sent a note asking you to meet on the granary roof. Torven Brumaren glances at the paper and waits for your answer.

journal.title: A life begins at birth
journal.text: Marei Laveno was born in The Beacon Cistern Arch to a serf family. The morning brought a quiet tide.

journal.title: A Small Beginning
journal.text: Bredel Laveno chooses to ask the visitor’s name before opening.

journal.title: The Small Hours
journal.text: You wake while the world is quiet, then drift away before it has finished waking. The hours belong to bodily needs rather than bells or promises.

journal.title: Steps Beyond Sight
journal.text: Footsteps pass somewhere beyond your view: near, then far, then gone. You turn toward the sound before there is a word for where it went.

journal.title: The Shape of a Hand
journal.text: A hand enters your small world. You study its shifting outline, then your own fingers, with the grave attention of someone meeting a mystery for the first time.

journal.title: A Cold Night
journal.text: Bredel Laveno chooses to take the shift and ask the neighbor to help.

journal.title: Light on the Wall
journal.text: A patch of light moves beyond your reach. Your eyes follow it until it breaks into shadow. No kingdom could be larger than that wall today.

journal.title: The Edge of Cloth
journal.text: Your fingers close around a fold of cloth. The rough weave, the warmth beneath it and the effort of holding on fill the whole moment.

journal.title: A hard winter
journal.text: The winter was long and the grain ran out before it did. Bredel Laveno ate last and least, and you learned what hunger does to a night.

journal.title: The Returning Shape
journal.text: A familiar shape leans close, disappears and returns. You cannot count the returns, but your body knows the difference between waiting and being held.

journal.title: Your First Words
journal.text: Bredel Laveno chooses to write down the unfamiliar word.

journal.title: A World of Breathing
journal.text: For now, the world comes as warmth, hunger and the rise and fall of nearby breathing. Beyond it, The Beacon Cistern Arch has names you cannot yet know.

journal.title: Before Words
journal.text: A voice repeats the same soft sounds. You do not know the story inside them; you know the pause before the voice begins again.

journal.title: A Low Note
journal.text: A low hum is easier to follow than speech. For a little while, each breath seems to carry the same note through the dark.

journal.title: Something to Show
journal.text: You build a little model.

journal.title: Someone Answers
journal.text: You hear an echo where a voice has already stopped. For a moment it seems another child has learned to speak from inside the stone. Old stories have plenty to say about that.

journal.title: Counting What Stays
journal.text: You count familiar shapes and lose your place when one moves. You begin again. There is comfort in a world that sometimes waits to be counted.

journal.title: The Unfinished Conversation
journal.text: Adult voices lower as you come near. The missing words leave room for a hundred explanations, most of them more fantastic than the truth is likely to be.

journal.title: Growing into your own life
journal.text: At 3, a year of games, small discoveries and learning the paths near home. Your survival developed through 365 actual focus days. Bredel Laveno remains part of those memories.

journal.title: The Best Chair

journal.title: The Cinderbound omen · age 4
journal.text: At four, a cold fireplace shows unfamiliar hands tending its coals. Only the person beside you sees you reach toward them.

journal.title: Play Outdoors

journal.title: A small pleasure
journal.text: Age 4, day 1463: You found 2 extra joy in making time for the people caring for you. Enjoyment follows what you actually do, and can return after 30 days.

journal.title: The Familiar Way of Speaking
journal.text: Bredel Laveno has a familiar rhythm of speech. The words may change, but a pause in just the right place can make an ordinary sentence sound like home.

journal.title: A conversation after the lamps go out
journal.text: You wake to Bredel Laveno and Talmund Laveno speaking in the next room. There is a traveling offer on the table and a cup gone cold beside it. “I never said forever,” Bredel Laveno says. Talmund Laveno lowers their voice when the floorboard creaks under your feet.

journal.title: A Familiar Name in the Day
journal.text: Torven Brumaren remains a living person in your world, beyond the last conversation you remember. A friendship contains separate days as well as the ones its people share.

journal.title: The place beside the window
journal.text: Cevra of Levvarel pulls a bench toward the window. Lomaya Kamedi puts a slate in the gap before anyone can sit down. Yesterday the two of them shared their lunch; today neither looks at the other. The rest of the table waits to see where you sit.

journal.text: Bellward child. The ward bells ring through a bread riot on the night you are born. Your household runs the communal oven; neighbors take turns guarding the door and feeding the queue. Marei Laveno, happy 6th birthday.

Tell me one thing you have learned because you wanted to, rather than because somebody set you a lesson. I would like to hear the whole explanation.

I am still learning how to be your parent as you become your own person.

My work as a cook gives me plenty to think about, but I wanted to make room for your birthday too.

— Bredel Laveno

I hope you find something this year that belongs to you: a skill, a friendship, or simply a place where you feel at ease.

We have not always found it easy to speak. I did not want this day to pass without a word; you need not find a reply before you are ready.

— Cevra of Levvarel

family_parent.speaker: family_parent
family_parent.text:
Marei Laveno, happy 6th birthday.

I hope this year brings a friend who enjoys your questions. You do not need to know the answer before you are allowed to ask.

I am proud to know you, even on the days neither of us knows quite what to say.

My work as a shrine keeper gives me plenty to think about, but I wanted to make room for your birthday too.

— Talmund Laveno

entries.title: A Letter from Bredel Laveno
entries.body:
Marei Laveno, happy 6th birthday.

Tell me one thing you have learned because you wanted to, rather than because somebody set you a lesson. I would like to hear the whole explanation.

I am still learning how to be your parent as you become your own person.

My work as a cook gives me plenty to think about, but I wanted to make room for your birthday too.

— Bredel Laveno

entries.title: A Letter from Torven Brumaren
entries.body:
Marei Laveno, happy 6th birthday.

I hope this year brings a friend who enjoys your questions. You do not need to know the answer before you are allowed to ask.

We have not always found it easy to speak. I did not want this day to pass without a word; you need not find a reply before you are ready.

— Torven Brumaren
